entries.summary: AWS read-only verification: fix approach proven valid in real Lambda env
entries.detail: Read-only AWS CLI (profile 081020446316_INTTRA-Dev-Engg, account 081020446316, us-east-1). The 4 handlers are AWS Lambda functions (java17, State=Active): inttra-int-lambda-visibility-outbound-poller (role INTTRA-INT-Visibility-Outbound-Lambda), -pending-start (role INTTRA-LAMBDA-INT-TT-PENDING-Start), -error-email (role inttra_int_visibility_error_email_lambda), -s3-archive (role INTTRA-LAMBDA-INT-TT-STREAM-S3). Each has an IAM execution role => Lambda injects AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET/SESSION_TOKEN env vars, resolved by DefaultCredentialsProvider's EnvironmentVariableCredentialsProvider. CloudWatch evidence: (1) /aws/lambda/...outbound-poller logs the exact 'CredentialsProvider must not be null' trace at HandlerSupport.getParameterStore:54 -> resolveSsmPath:62 -> VisibilityOutboundPoller.<init> (root cause confirmed live). (2) ...error-email logs same error via ParameterStoreResolver.<init>:30 -> util.HandlerSupport.setClientIdAndClientSecret:86 -> createInjector -> VisibilityErrorEmail.<init> (matches the ParameterStoreResolver patch). (3) ...s3-archive Jul-18 log: 'S3StorageClient: Resolved AWS credentials using provider: DefaultCredentialsProvider(providerChain=[SystemProperty, EnvironmentVariable, WebIdentityToken, Profile(default), Container, InstanceProfile])' => runtime PROOF DefaultCredentialsProvider resolves the execution-role creds in real Lambda. s3-archive runtime OK; its issue is the Sonar coverage gate. (4) ...pending-start had no cred error. Conclusion: the bugfix/ION-16387 approach (explicit region + AwsCredentialsProviderWrapper.of(DefaultCredentialsProvider.create())) is valid and WILL work in the real AWS Lambda environment.

entries.summary: Lambda creds = execution-role STS creds injected as reserved runtime env vars (not configured env), resolved by SDK2 EnvironmentVariableCredentialsProvider; ECS uses ContainerCredentialsProvider
entries.detail: Lambda credential mechanism clarified (user correctly noted no cred env vars in config). CONFIRMED via read-only AWS CLI: the 4 lambdas' CONFIGURED Environment.Variables contain ONLY app vars (outboundIpfSqs, pendingSqsUrl, s3ArchiveBucket, dynamoDbEnv, env, dbUrl, etc.) - NO AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET/SESSION_TOKEN. Credentials are NOT stored there. Instead: (a) each function has an IAM execution role; role INTTRA-LAMBDA-INT-TT-STREAM-S3 trust policy allows only Principal Service lambda.amazonaws.com to sts:AssumeRole. (b) At invocation, the AWS Lambda runtime assumes the execution role and injects the temporary STS creds as RESERVED runtime environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_REGION) - these are set by the platform and are NOT visible in get-function-configuration. (c) AWS SDK 2.x DefaultCredentialsProvider chain [SystemProperty, EnvironmentVariable, WebIdentityToken, Profile(default), Container, InstanceProfile] resolves them via EnvironmentVariableCredentialsProvider (2nd in chain). CONTRAST: ECS service modules use AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI -> ContainerCredentialsProvider (5th) hitting 169.254.170.2 to fetch the TASK role creds. Both are temporary role creds, different delivery/provider. KEY: the bug was NOT cred availability; BaseAwsConfig.validateNotNull only checks the CredentialsProvider OBJECT is non-null at build time. develop passed none -> failed. Fix passes DefaultCredentialsProvider.create() (a lazy non-null provider) which at runtime resolves the injected env-var creds. Runtime proof: s3-archive CloudWatch 2026-07-18 'Resolved AWS credentials using provider: DefaultCredentialsProvider(...)'.

entries.summary: Timeline: migration live ~2026-07-16, still broken today; only paramstore-using lambdas (outbound-poller,error-email) error; createDefault* helpers spared pending-start & s3-archive
entries.detail: Deployment/log timeline + why only 2 of 4 lambdas error (authoritative, from cloud-sdk source + CloudWatch). ROOT of the per-lambda difference = which cloud-sdk factory each uses on develop: (1) outbound-poller & error-email build AwsParameterStoreConfig.builder().region().build() (via ParameterStoreClientFactory.createParameterStore / ParameterStoreResolver). AwsParameterStoreConfig.build() runs BaseAwsConfig validation which MANDATES a non-null credentialsProvider; the migration set region but not credentials -> throws 'CredentialsProvider must not be null'. There is NO createDefault param-store helper. (2) pending-start uses MessagingClientFactory.createDefaultStringClient() and s3-archive uses StorageClientFactory.createDefaultS3Client(); both helpers internally call DefaultCredentialsProvider.create() (messaging) or SDK default (storage) and BYPASS the strict AwsXxxConfig/BaseAwsConfig validation -> they always had a provider -> never threw. TIMELINE: broken AWS 2.x migration went live ~2026-07-16 (outbound-poller first error 2026-07-16 16:41Z; error-email first 2026-07-17 00:10Z). s3-archive's 2026-07-18 'Resolved AWS credentials' success log is the SAME migrated code via the working createDefaultS3Client path. Functions were re-deployed 2026-07-29/30 but with the still-broken code (fix on bugfix/ION-16387 not merged): outbound-poller STILL erroring 8736x in last 4 days (latest 2026-07-30 16:46:40Z, after its 07-30 12:57Z redeploy); error-email STILL erroring 17x (latest 2026-07-30 00:13:31Z; sparse because event-driven, vs outbound-poller which polls constantly). pending-start & s3-archive: 0 cred errors ever. STS = AWS Security Token Service: issues TEMPORARY creds (ASIA-prefixed accessKeyId + secretKey + sessionToken + expiry) when a role is assumed; Lambda exec-role creds and ECS task-role creds are both STS temp creds. The fix makes all four explicit/consistent.

entries.summary: Corrected doc: DynamoDB must use cloud-sdk DatabaseRepository/DynamoRepositoryFactory, not raw DynamoDbClient; s3-archiver raw client is the documented exception
entries.detail: Corrected the AWS-pending doc's DynamoDB guidance after user pointed out raw DynamoDbClient was wrong. cloud-sdk DOES provide a DynamoDB abstraction: com.inttra.mercury.cloudsdk.database.api.DatabaseRepository<T,ID> created via DynamoRepositoryFactory.createRepository/createEnhancedRepository/createStandardRepository(DynamoDbClientConfig, table, EntityClass, DynamoRepositoryConfig). Entities use cloud-sdk @Table + v2 Enhanced @DynamoDbBean/@DynamoDbPartitionKey/@DynamoDbSortKey/@DynamoDbConvertedBy (verified in booking BookingDetail). Standard pattern across ALL migrated modules via *Dao + Guice *DynamoModule (auth TokenDao/AuthDynamoModule, booking BookingDetailDao/BookingDynamoModule, network SubscriptionsDao, registration RegistrationDao, rates, VAS, webbl, visibility ContainerEventDao, booking-bridge, bill-of-lading-v2). For generic raw-item access (Map<String,AttributeValue>, no entity) use DynamoRepositoryFactory.createDynamoDbClient(DynamoDbClientConfig) -> a configured low-level v2 DynamoDbClient (region+creds validated same as BaseAwsConfig). The 'other module' the user referred to = visibility-s3-archiver HandlerSupport.getDynamoDbClient() which hand-builds a raw DynamoDbClient (documented rationale: generic raw-item DynamoDB Streams read with no entity-based cloud-sdk equivalent); recommended follow-up to route it through createDynamoDbClient(config) for uniform region/creds/retry. Updated doc: mapping table (2 rows: entity vs raw), §C lambda DynamoDB bullet, §1.3.1 DynamoSparkService bullet, and new §E. NOTE: working tree is currently on develop (0334766084) - reflog shows an external checkout develop + pull (shared environment, not me); bugfix/ION-16387 intact at 53e54c5482 (local==origin), fix safe and pushed.
